components.name: Hero Number
components.description: The phone number as the hero: display type with a red rule.

narrative.overview: A barbershop in Skien needs one thing from its website: a phone number you can read from across the street. The page is printed, not decorated: warm paper, navy ink, one red, a handful of fixed shapes. The voice is spoken and local.
keyCharacteristics: The phone number is the largest thing on the first screen and is a link.
Two inks on paper: sign ink and pole red; blue only inside the pole and as the focus ring on paper.
One pressable shape (the key) with a hard lip that collapses when pressed.
Prices and opening hours share one ink plate; contact is one flat red band.
No italics, no brass, no pills.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink and red do the work; no third accent color enters this system.

rules.name: The Stripe Is Trim Rule
rules.body: Red and blue appear together only inside the pole and as the thin stripe between hero and plate.

rules.name: The Paper Is Printed Rule
rules.body: The page ground is warm and slightly grainy, set as a background; the grain never overlays content.

rules.name: The Roman Rule
rules.body: There is no italic anywhere; emphasis comes from weight and size.

rules.name: The Real Ø Rule
rules.body: Norwegian text must render æ, ø and å in the same face as its neighbours; check any label face with 'LØRDAG'.

rules.name: The Plain Speech Rule
rules.body: Copy is short and spoken; a sentence that could sit on any barbershop's site goes.

rules.name: The Hard Offset Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is offset 4px, solid and never blurred; key lips are ink, plates and the sign cast red.

dos: Do keep the phone number (46 15 91 57) the largest element on the first screen, and keep the address and walk-in line within one thumb scroll.
Do use pole red for calling, the number's rule, the map pin and the contact band only.
Do make every pressable thing a key or an underlined text link; press moves 4px down in 120ms.
Do keep shadows hard and offset 4px, in ink (keys) or red (plates).
Do keep above-the-fold content independent of scroll; it enters on load in 300ms or less.
Do use a paper focus ring on ink and red surfaces; blue is for paper.
Do check any new label face against "LØRDAG" and the digits 0-9 before adopting it.
donts: Don't use italics, brass or gold, or pill-shaped buttons.
Don't put kicker or eyebrow labels above headings; the heading carries its own weight.
Don't use unicode glyphs as icons; draw inline SVG in one filled style (phone and map pin today).
Don't use blurred drop shadows, gradient text, or a texture over content.
Don't add photos, reviews, awards or prices that have not been confirmed; example values stay visibly flagged.
Don't repeat brochure copy that could sit on any barbershop site.
Don't use Barlow Condensed (wide Ø) or Bodoni Moda (hairlines vanish at small sizes); both were tried and removed.
